transcript:
User: Yeah I saw your thing online. Honestly this smells like one of those AI scam gadgets. Convince me it's not garbage.
Agent: Totally fair reaction — there’s a lot of junk out there right now.  

I’ll keep it simple: our system only has one job — when someone calls your business and you can’t pick up, it still grabs the lead, books the appointment or captures the info, and gets it to you so you don’t lose the revenue from that call.  

Before I go further, what kind of business are you running?
User: Ortiz Roofing in Dallas. How do I know this isn’t some robot calling my customers and spamming them?
Agent: Got it, Ortiz Roofing in Dallas — makes sense you’re protective of your customers.  

Two things: 1) our system **only talks to people who already called you** (no cold spam, ever), and 2) it sounds like a real receptionist on *your* line, answering missed calls and after-hours calls so those storm and leak jobs don’t go to the next roofer.  

What’s your bigger worry — sounding “robotic” to homeowners, or losing control of who’s being called and when?
User: I’m worried about losing control. How do I know this isn’t recorded and who sees my data?
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense — if you lose control of calls and data, it’s not worth it.  

Here’s how we handle it: calls are recorded the same way a normal phone system records them, they’re encrypted, and access is limited to your team and our small implementation team for support — we don’t sell, share, or repurpose your call data, and everything stays tied to **your** phone numbers and customers, not some shared database.  

When a storm hits and calls spike, what’s happening today — are you personally missing calls, or is it your office/answering service?
User: I’m the one missing calls when I’m up on a roof. How do I know you’re not selling data?
Agent: Gotcha — you’re on the roof, calls are slipping, and you don’t want your customer list ending up in someone else’s hands.  

Plain and simple: we **do not** sell, rent, or trade your data — no lead brokering, no sharing between contractors, nothing; your call recordings and customer info are only used to answer your calls, send you the summaries, and support your account, and we’re happy to put that in writing in the agreement if you move forward.  

When you miss a call now — say during a hail week — do those people usually leave a voicemail, or do they just call the next roofer?
User: They rarely leave voicemails. Most folks just move on to the next roofer. What’s your plan for that?
Agent: Right, so every time you’re on a roof and can’t grab it, you’re basically feeding the next roofer work.  

Our plan is: when you miss a call, our system answers **right away** in your name, grabs their info and job details, can even quote basics or book an inspection slot on your calendar, then texts/emails you the summary so that lead is locked to Ortiz Roofing before they can shop around.  

If we could reliably catch even, say, 5 of those a week and turn them into booked estimates, would that be meaningful for you, or is your call volume higher than that?
User: So, you’re saying 5 booked jobs a week? How do I know this isn’t just a fancy sales pitch?
Agent: Totally fair to question that — I’m not promising a magic number, I’m saying even 5 a week *if* your volume supports it would already be meaningful.  

The real test is simple: we turn it on, it only answers your real missed calls, and you watch how many actual inspection appointments and qualified leads it captures over a short trial window — if it doesn’t put real opportunities on your calendar, you shut it off.  

Roughly how many calls do you think you’re missing in a normal week right now?
User: About 30 calls a week. But how do I know this isn't just sucking more money out of my pocket?
Agent: Makes sense you’re cautious — if it just becomes another bill, it’s useless.  

With ~30 calls a week, even if you’re only missing a third, that’s 10 people; if our system doesn’t turn enough of those into real inspection appointments to clearly pay for itself, you’d turn it off — the whole point is that one closed roof should more than cover the monthly cost.  

Would you be open to a short demo call where we walk through your numbers and let you see exactly how it would handle an Ortiz Roofing caller, before you decide anything?
User: Alright, show me this demo call. But I’m not giving you my final decision today. What's the next step?
Agent: Totally fine, you don’t need to decide on the spot — the goal is just to see it in action with your numbers.  

Next step is a short Zoom where Jay (our founder) walks you through how it would handle an Ortiz Roofing missed call, shows what you’d actually see on your phone, and runs the math on your 30 missed calls a week so you can decide later if it’s worth it.  

When do you usually have a quieter window — mornings or late afternoons?
User: Late afternoons work best. But remember, I’m only agreeing to see the live call, not signing up.
Agent: Totally hear you — this is just to *see* it, not to sign anything.  

Let’s pick a late afternoon — would, say, this Thursday around 4:00 your time work, or is another day better for you?
User: Thursday at 4:00 sounds fine. Remember, I'm just seeing the demo, not committing to anything.
Agent: Perfect, Thursday at 4:00 it is — and yes, totally understood, it’s just a demo so you can see if it’s worth it for Ortiz Roofing, no commitment.  

What’s the best email to send the Zoom link and a quick reminder to?
User: Send it to ortizroofing@gmail.com. Remember, I’m only checking the demo, no commitments yet.
Agent: Got it, I’ll have the Zoom invite for Thursday at 4:00 sent to ortizroofing@gmail.com so you can just check out the demo, no commitments at all. If anything changes or you don’t see the link, you can just reply to that email. Really glad you reached out today — talk to you Thursday, and have a good one out there on the roofs.

The agent confirmed the demo and collected the user's email for the Zoom invite.
